about: THE 42 ROWS, in order, in their 8 groups and 3 sections (PART D under BUILD ITEMS A AND B, the owner 2026-10-21). was: the old row numbers 1..48 (old_rows) a row came from. when: WHEN THE ROUND RUNS THE ROW: "every round"; "daily HH:MM" or "nightly HH:MM" (each round from that hour on, until the day ends at the reset, 07:00); "on the owner's word" (never by the round).
groups_about: THE TWO GROUPS OF A RED ROW (the owner 2026-10-24: "we have two groups and it should be clear. group 1 the thing to fix is in the virtual_workspace it has access can automatically go fix it. group 2 the agent itself is broken and this should require an unlock"). WORKSPACE: the cause is under the workspace (settings reads.workspace): the red-row fix loop fixes it by itself, a fixer per red row at once. AGENT: the cause is under ~/virtual_sanity (settings reads.sanity), the agent itself: healed only while the master lock is OPEN by his press (settings master.mark). SORTED FROM THE RECORDS, NEVER A LIST OF ROWS (the owner: "make sure its dynamic and not hard coded because all are changing constantly"): agent_words, the round's own first words for a row whose program failed; a BROKEN file's path root; a fixer's last word AGENT. A step only his hands can do (a PIN, a seal, a GO, a secret, live data) stays red with his step in either group, never counted as forced. A row's own keys here, read each round: container; chain false (no piece of the night's chain: its red is never held on the chain); app (the app its facts come from, built by the hot fix utility: iphone, macos); own_fix (a subcommand of the row's own program, run before any hired fixer once its ready() says so); stop (the night step whose stop is this row's fault, as the rows name it); measure (the detector's measure taken again when a fixer's turn ends); rerun (a chain or steps of the night run again: his 3 minute line when the loop has no word; note: words before the line); step (a line of his own).

x_about: THE X BOARD (the owner 2026-10-22: "make a military style x board ... a big black x for items done ... based on the group of the row and the list of rows per group and by day and by release for release"; "verify the list in the description matches the list exactly with nothing else"): one line per group; WHAT MAKES ITS X is exactly its own rows, by name, read from this file, nothing else; its X when every one of them is green for the day shown; the release group's X only for the release: from its release day (settings scrum.release) on, its rows green.

x_rule.about: WHAT AN X MEANS (the owner 2026-10-22: "do we have a summary? do we have a working standup? do we have a functional live?"; "yes = x"): a row counts toward its group's X when it did its own job today: a run of today that ended and measured or delivered something, whatever the colour of what it found; a run that says one of not_done did not do its job. A step of the night and the release (passed) count only when the run passed (green): their job is to pass. Once a row counted today it stays counted until the day ends. The release's X only from its release day on.

waiting.about: A GROUP WHOSE WORK COMES IN (the owner 2026-10-22: "if i asked for 1 new item today the x should go away for the build today"): its X also needs no request still before its end, in one of these states; a new request takes the X away until it is through.

x_says_about: EACH GROUP'S BOLD LINE ON THE X BOARD (the owner's own words, 2026-10-22: "they can be there all the time fixed"; "not dynamic to show up"): what its X stands for, always shown under the group's rows; the X beside it says whether it is so.
